steps.title: Prepare flow cytometry reagents
steps.instruction: Make 2 % FBS in PBS (FCS buffer) by adding 1 mL fetal bovine serum to 50 mL Milli‑Q water; freshly prepare 1× permeabilization buffer by mixing 200 µL 10× permeabilization buffer with 1 800 µL FCS buffer.

steps.title: Extract viral RNA from infected BHK‑21 cells
steps.instruction: Harvest BHK‑21 cells infected with rVSV‑dG‑RV‑G‑GFP or rVSV‑GFP‑WT and extract total viral RNA according to the method described in step 33 (molecular characterization, RT‑PCR) during days 1–4.

steps.title: Generate standard curve and set up one‑step RT‑qPCR
steps.instruction: Prepare ten‑fold RNA dilutions (0.1–1000 ng) for the standard curve; on ice assemble a 50 µL reaction per well containing 1 µL 2× SuperScript III RT/Platinum Taq Mix, 25 µL 10 µM forward primer, 1 µL 10 µM reverse primer, 0.5 µL 10 µM fluorogenic probe, 1 µL RNase OUT, 10 µL RNA template (1 pg–1 µg), and nuclease‑free water to 50 µL. Seal plates with adhesive film, briefly centrifuge, and run on a CFX96 with the program: 50 °C 15 min, 95 °C 2 min, then 40 cycles of 95 °C 15 s and 60 °C 30 s, followed by a melt curve from 65 °C to 95 °C increasing 0.5 °C per step.

steps.title: Analyze RT‑qPCR data and quantify viral RNA
steps.instruction: In Excel plot log₁₀ RNA quantity (X‑axis) versus Ct (Y‑axis) for each virus to obtain a linear regression (e.g., Y = −3.1452 X + 21.74); compute efficiency as e = (10^(−1/slope) − 1) × 100. Infect BHK‑21 cells at 70–80 % confluence with each virus at MOI = 1, collect supernatants at 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42 h post‑infection, extract RNA, run the RT‑qPCR as above, calculate copy number using T = 10^{(Ct − b)/m}, take log₁₀ of T, and plot growth curves in GraphPad Prism.

substeps.instruction: Day 1: Seed 5 × 10⁴ BHK‑21 cells per well on glass coverslips in a 24‑well plate; incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ overnight.
Day 2: Wash cells with 1× PBS, add virus diluted in infection medium to achieve MOI = 1, incubate 37 °C for 2 h with gentle shaking; wash 3× with PBS, add 0.5–1 mL growth medium.
Day 3: Verify GFP expression, wash 3× with 200 µL 1× PBS, fix with 200 µL 4 % PFA at 22–25 °C for 1 h, wash PBS, permeabilize with 200 µL 0.1 % Triton X‑100 for 10 min, wash 3× PBS (5 min each).
Block with 200 µL blocking buffer for 1 h at 22–25 °C on a shaker.
Prepare primary antibody (VSV‑M or RV‑G) at 1:400: dilute 3 µL antibody in 1 200 µL 0.5 % BSA; add 200 µL per well and incubate 18 ± 2 h at 4 °C on a shaker, protected from light.

Day 4: Wash 3× PBS (5 min each), prepare secondary antibody (goat anti‑mouse IgG Alexa‑Fluor 488) at 1:800: dilute 1.5 µL secondary in 1 200 µL 0.5 % BSA; add 200 µL per well, incubate 1–2 h at 22–25 °C on a shaker, foil.
Wash 3× PBS (5 min), rinse once with distilled water, aspirate.
Stain nuclei with 200 µL DAPI (1:10 000) for 30 min on ice, foil.

Mount coverslips on glass slides with one drop VECTASHIELD, label, dip coverslips in Milli‑Q water, dry edges on lint‑free paper, invert so cells face down, press gently with a 1 µL tip, seal corners with clear nail polish, dry 30 min in dark, store at 4 °C protected from light (image within 2 weeks).
Acquire images on a Zeiss LSM880 confocal microscope and analyze with ZenCore 3.4.

steps.title: Flow cytometry analysis of GFP expression

substeps.instruction: Day 1: Seed 0.3 × 10⁶ BHK‑21 cells per well in six‑well plates; incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ overnight.

Day 2: When cells reach 70–80 % confluence, infect triplicate wells with rVSV‑dG‑RV‑G‑GFP or rVSV‑GFP‑WT at MOI = 1; include three mock‑infected wells. Incubate 2 h at 37 °C with shaking every 15–20 min, then remove inoculum, wash 3× with PBS, add 1.5 mL growth medium.
Day 4 (30 h post‑infection): Remove supernatant, wash cells with PBS, detach cells using PBS only, transfer to labeled 1.5 mL tubes.
Centrifuge 300 × g for 5 min, discard supernatant, wash pellet with PBS.
Prepare live/dead stain: mix 2 µL LIVE/DEAD Fixable Violet with 2 mL FCS buffer (2 % FBS in PBS); add 200 µL to each cell pellet, incubate on ice 30 min protected from light.
Pellet cells, wash once with PBS, add 200 µL 1× permeabilization buffer, incubate on ice 15 min protected from light.
Centrifuge, wash once with PBS, resuspend cells in 100 µL FCS buffer.

Run samples on a CytoFLEX flow cytometer: perform QC with calibration beads, acquire 30 000–50 000 events per sample in tube mode, apply gating sequence (SSC‑A vs PB450‑A for live cells; FSC‑A vs FSC‑H for singlets; SSC‑A vs FITC‑A for GFP‑positive cells).
Export data, analyze with CytExpert or FCS Express, and plot GFP‑positive percentages and mean fluorescence intensities.

description: Vesicular stomatitis virus (VSV), the prototype member of the family Rhabdoviridae, is a non-segmented, negative strand RNA virus. The VSV genome is 11-kb, and it encodes five structural genes including: nucleoprotein (N), phosphoprotein (P), matrix (M), glycoprotein (G), and large polymerase (L).1 Owing to its capability of stable maintenance and expression of transgenes, VSV has been demonstrated as an efficient system for generating recombinant vaccines against viruses of animal and human origins.2 Additionally, VSV offers a versatile tool to study virus host interactions due to its wide host spectrum.3 Rabies is a highly fatal disease, caused by rabies virus (RV), and is responsible for approximately 59,000 human deaths annually.4 The remarkably diverse reservoir species of RV render its control and prevention challenging. However, a substantial decrease in human rabies cases could be achieved through development of novel vaccines targeting RV reservoirs. To study the role of the RV-G in RV entry and its interaction with the cellular receptors. Herein, we describe a reverse genetics system based on the generation of VSV in which the G gene of VSV is replaced by a reporter gene (green fluorescent protein, GFP) together with the heterologous RV-G gene. This protocol describes the sequential process to successfully manipulate the VSV genome and to clone transgenes in compatibility (Figure 1A). The pVSV-dG-GFP-2.6 vector which encodes the antigenomic cDNA of VSV, can be manipulated to insert a transgene (exemplified here with full-length open reading frame (ORF) of the rabies virus surface glycoprotein (RV-G), derived from the Egyptian strain isolate (GenBank accession number: MK760770.1) (Figure 1B). The RV-G is inserted in the multiple cloning sites of pVSV-dG-GFP-2.6 (recipient plasmid) between the M and the GFP genes using unique MluI and NheI restriction sites.
